headline: Two players placed on NHL waivers for Oct. 23
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that defensemen Daemon Hunt of the Wild and Jack St. Ivany of the Jets have been placed on NHL waivers for Oct. 23 and are available to be claimed.

Hunt's numbers explain why Minnesota is willing to let him go. In 11 games so far this season he has no points, averaging 14.14 minutes a night. At five-on-five, the Wild controlled just 41% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality) with him on the ice, and the team's share was about 19 percentage points better when he sat. St. Ivany's sample is only four games so far this season, so it says little either way. Winnipeg held 47% of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team did slightly better, by about 2 points, when he played. Neither has a goal this season, and neither has been creating much offense on his own: each projects at 0.18 expected goals per 60 minutes. For a team claiming one, that makes either player a depth defender, not a fix. Hunt's on-ice results are the weaker of the two.
